svg.text: THE QUALITIES · the steep curve beats the tall one

text.tspan: Power, speed and agility are one physics problem: how fast you turn force on,
not how much you have. You get ~0.1–0.3 s of ground contact — train the slope.

svg.text: THE RFD OSCILLOSCOPE — force vs time (ms)
the only time you actually have
tall, slow — peaks after the window
RFD = ΔForce ÷ Δtime = the SLOPE, not the peak.
you don't have time to reach max force — you have 0.1–0.3 s.
strength + plyo beats either alone. You can't express force you don't have.
THREE FLAVOURS OF FAST — one engine, three tuned outputs
ONE ENGINE — phosphagen system + Type IIx fibres
explosive force in place — force × velocity
power applied to locomotion — two skills
10–30 m · sled / hill · lean · long drive
3 REACTIVE — respond to a stimulus (true agility)
⚠ 5-10-5 = a COD test, not agility — no reaction
THE ELASTIC ENGINE — the stretch-shortening cycle & how to read it
STRETCH-SHORTENING CYCLE — a stretched rubber band
early gains are NEURAL — recruit Type IIx + fire them earlier / faster (rate coding), not new tissue.
RSI GAUGE — which tool do you need?
THE SAFETY INTERLOCK — earn the right to be explosive
GATE INPUTS — all three must be satisfied
depth jumps · max sprints — locked until the gate opens
pogos · squat jumps · low box jumps — these pass freely

text.tspan: your joints in a fraction of

svg.text: vertical ↑ · broad ↑ · 10 m ↓ · flying 20–30 m ↓ · 5-10-5 ↓ · RSI ↑
POWER = STRENGTH EXPRESSED FAST — you can't express force you don't have.
strength climbing but jumps / sprints flat? → you have force, not RATE — add full-intent explosive work.
